title: Reporting a Leak to the Letting Agency
context: A tenant telephones a letting agency about water coming through a bedroom ceiling and arranges for a plumber to visit.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Good afternoon, Halstead Property Management. Sanjay speaking.

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: Hello. I'm ringing about a leak at the flat I rent through you. It's 14b Wexford Road.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Let me pull up the file. Wexford Road... is that the top flat?

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: That's right, 14b, top floor.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Right, thank you. I remember your flat, lovely view from the top there.

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: It is, usually — not so much today with all this rain, though.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Here we are. And your name, just so I've got it on the record?

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: Dana Whitlock.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Thank you, Ms Whitlock. Can you tell me exactly what's happening?

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: There's water coming through the ceiling in the back bedroom. There's a brown patch about the size of a dinner plate, and it's definitely getting bigger.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Oh no, that doesn't sound good at all. Let me get a few more details down.

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: It's honestly a bit stressful. I keep going in to check on it.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: And when did you first notice it?

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: Monday. No — hang on, that's not right. It was Sunday night, because I remember the football was on. Sunday.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Sunday. Is it dripping at the moment, or just damp?

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: It was dripping this morning. I've put a bucket underneath it.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: That's exactly the right thing to do. Is the flat above yours occupied?

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: I think so, but nobody answers the door. I've knocked twice now.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Okay, don't worry about that part, we have a master key for the building if we need it.

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: Oh good, I didn't realise that.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Leave that with us, we'll deal with that end. I'm logging this as a category two repair, which means somebody has to attend within three working days.

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: So not today, then.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: I'm afraid not. It would only be category one — same day — if the ceiling itself were coming down. The plumbers we use are a firm called Ridgeway, and they'll ring you directly to fix a time.

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: Ridgeway. Are they the same people who came about the boiler?

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: No, that was a different firm. Ridgeway do everything on the water side.

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: All right. I'm at work Tuesday and Wednesday, but Thursday I'm at home all day. And Friday morning as well.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: I'll put Thursday down as your preference — actually, hold on. Thursday is when Ridgeway are doing the whole block on Preston Street. Could you manage Friday morning instead?

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: Friday morning is fine, yes.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Friday morning it is. Now, do you want to be there yourself, or shall we let them in with our set of keys?

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: I'd rather be there, if that's all right. I want to hear what they say about it.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Perfectly reasonable. There is one thing I have to ask you, though. Please don't switch on the light in that room. If water has got anywhere near the wiring, turning it on is genuinely dangerous. Use a lamp on the other side of the room instead.

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: I hadn't even thought of that. I'll leave it off.

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: Is that likely, do you think, getting worse before then?

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Hopefully not. The bucket should manage most of it, but it's best you know what to do just in case.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Good. And if things get worse over the weekend — if the ceiling starts to sag, or the water reaches a socket — ring the out-of-hours line. It's the same number you've just called, but you press 9 rather than waiting for the options.

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: Press 9. Right, I've written that down.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: One last thing, and I'd rather say it now than have you find out later. The repair itself costs you nothing — it's a structural problem, so it's the landlord's responsibility. But if the plumber turns up and nobody is in, there's a missed appointment fee of 45 pounds, and that does come out of your deposit.

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: I'll be there, don't worry. What about the ceiling itself? It looks ruined.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: The plasterer comes after the plumber, usually about a fortnight later, once everything has dried out properly. There's no sense in painting a wet ceiling.

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: That makes sense. Thank you for your help.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: You're welcome. Is there anything else at all I can help with today?

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: No, I think that covers everything, thank you.

script.speaker: Agent
script.text: Not at all. Your reference for this is 8072 — quote that if you need to ring again.

script.speaker: Tenant
script.text: 8072. Thanks very much. Goodbye.

questions.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

questions.explanation: The tenant gives the address at the start of the call: "It's 14b Wexford Road," and later confirms it is the top floor.
The tenant says Monday, then corrects herself: "that's not right. It was Sunday night, because I remember the football was on."
The agent says, "I'm logging this as a category two repair, which means somebody has to attend within three working days." Category one is same-day.
The agent names the firm: "The plumbers we use are a firm called Ridgeway." A different firm dealt with the boiler.
Thursday is suggested first, but the agent stops himself because the firm is elsewhere, and asks, "Could you manage Friday morning instead?"

questions.sentence: Charge if nobody is at home for the visit: £___
questions.explanation: The repair is free, but the agent warns there is "a missed appointment fee of 45 pounds, and that does come out of your deposit."

questions.instruction: Answer the questions below. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

questions.question: What has the tenant put under the leak?
questions.explanation: The tenant says, "It was dripping this morning. I've put a bucket underneath it," and the agent tells her that was the right thing to do.

questions.question: Which room is the water coming into?
questions.explanation: She describes "water coming through the ceiling in the back bedroom," with a brown patch that is getting bigger.

questions.question: What must the tenant not switch on in that room?
questions.explanation: The agent warns, "Please don't switch on the light in that room," because water near the wiring makes it dangerous.

questions.question: Which number must be pressed to reach the out-of-hours line?
questions.explanation: The out-of-hours line uses the same telephone number, but the agent says "you press 9 rather than waiting for the options."
